packet.description_seed: Former President Zuma's trip to India reignites anger over a decade-old corruption scandal.

what: Zuma showing South Africa 'middle finger' by meeting Gupta brother - minister

clean_source_blocks.text: Jacob Zuma has reportedly said he wants to stand for election again Former President Jacob Zuma is "showing the middle finger" to South Africa, a minister in the country has said after it emerged Zuma had met one of the Indian businessmen allegedly at the heart of a huge corruption scandal. A photograph of Zuma and Ajay Gupta in an Indian temple was shared by Indian media this week. Around a decade ago, the Gupta brothers were accused of profiting from their close links to then-President Zuma and influencing South African policy. Both parties denied wrongdoing, while the family left South Africa in 2018 after a judicial commission began investigating allegations they were involved in massive fraud, known as "state capture". South African authorities cancelled their arrest warrant for Ajay Gupta the following year.

Former President Jacob Zuma is "showing the middle finger" to South Africa, a minister in the country has said after it emerged Zuma had met one of the Indian businessmen allegedly at the heart of a huge corruption scandal. A photograph of Zuma and Ajay Gupta in an Indian temple was shared by Indian media this week. Around a decade ago, the Gupta brothers were accused of profiting from their close links to then-President Zuma and influencing South African policy. Both parties denied wrongdoing, while the family left South Africa in 2018 after a judicial commission began investigating allegations they were involved in massive fraud, known as "state capture". South African authorities cancelled their arrest warrant for Ajay Gupta the following year.

The two younger Gupta brothers, Atul and Rajesh, went to the United Arab Emirates where a court in 2023 turned down a South African request to extradite them. In a press briefing on Friday, cabinet minister Khumbudzo Ntshavheni said it was "very disturbing that a former state president openly and unapologetically shows the middle finger to South Africans who have lost a lot of money through the Gupta brothers' shenanigans". Zuma, a long-standing member of the African National Congress (ANC), was forced out of office in 2018 following a string of corruption allegations. He has always denied any wrongdoing. After meeting Ajay Gupta at the temple in India, Zuma, who now heads the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) party, reportedly said he would stand for re-election in South Africa's next elections.
Former President Zuma's trip to India reignites anger over a decade-old corruption scandal.

Former President Jacob Zuma is "showing the middle finger" to South Africa, a minister in the country has said after it emerged Zuma had met one of the Indian businessmen allegedly at the heart of a huge corruption scandal.

A photograph of Zuma and Ajay Gupta in an Indian temple was shared by Indian media this week.

Around a decade ago, the Gupta brothers were accused of profiting from their close links to then-President Zuma and influencing South African policy.

Both parties denied wrongdoing, while the family left South Africa in 2018 after a judicial commission began investigating allegations they were involved in massive fraud, known as "state capture".

South African authorities cancelled their arrest warrant for Ajay Gupta the following year.

The two younger Gupta brothers, Atul and Rajesh, went to the United Arab Emirates where a court in 2023 turned down a South African request to extradite them.

In a press briefing on Friday, cabinet minister Khumbudzo Ntshavheni said it was "very disturbing that a former state president openly and unapologetically shows the middle finger to South Africans who have lost a lot of money through the Gupta brothers' shenanigans".

Zuma, a long-standing member of the African National Congress (ANC), was forced out of office in 2018 following a string of corruption allegations. He has always denied any wrongdoing.

After meeting Ajay Gupta at the temple in India, Zuma, who now heads the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) party, reportedly said he would stand for re-election in South Africa's next elections.

In response, Ntshavheni said 84-year-old Zuma "continues to show a middle finger and claim that he wants to run this country again".

She also said it was a "disgrace" that the South African high commissioner to India, Anil Sooklal, had accompanied Zuma to the meeting with Gupta.

South Africa will launch an investigation into the meeting, international relations minister Ronald Lamola said.

payload.title: Jacob Zuman tapaaminen Ajay Guptan kanssa herätti uuden kiistan Etelä-Afrikassa
payload.summary: Etelä-Afrikan entisen presidentin Jacob Zuman tapaaminen Ajay Guptan kanssa Intiassa on nostanut uudelleen esiin maan laajan korruptioskandaalin. Ministeri Khumbudzo Ntshavheni arvosteli Zuman toimintaa poikkeuksellisen jyrkästi.
payload.content:
Etelä-Afrikan entinen presidentti Jacob Zuma on joutunut uuden arvostelun kohteeksi sen jälkeen, kun intialaisessa mediassa julkaistiin kuva hänestä Ajay Guptan kanssa intialaisessa temppelissä. Gupta kuuluu liikemiesperheeseen, jota on syytetty hyötymisestä läheisistä suhteistaan Zumaan ja vaikutusvallasta Etelä-Afrikan politiikkaan hänen presidenttikautensa aikana.

## Ministeri arvosteli tapaamista jyrkästi

Etelä-Afrikan hallituksen ministeri Khumbudzo Ntshavheni sanoi perjantain tiedotustilaisuudessa, että Zuman toiminta oli hyvin häiritsevää. Hänen mukaansa entinen valtionpäämies suhtautui avoimesti ja anteeksipyytelemättä halveksivasti eteläafrikkalaisiin, jotka ovat menettäneet paljon rahaa Gupta-veljesten toiminnan vuoksi.

Tapaaminen on herättänyt suuttumusta, koska Gupta-veljekset olivat keskeisiä nimiä niin sanotussa valtion kaappaukseksi kutsutussa korruptiovyyhdissä. Noin vuosikymmen sitten veljeksiä syytettiin siitä, että he hyötyivät yhteyksistään silloiseen presidenttiin Zumaan ja vaikuttivat maan päätöksentekoon. Zuma ja Gupta-perhe ovat kiistäneet väärinkäytökset.

## Korruptioskandaalin varjo jatkuu

Gupta-perhe lähti Etelä-Afrikasta vuonna 2018, kun oikeudellinen komissio alkoi tutkia väitteitä laajasta petos- ja korruptiotoiminnasta. Etelä-Afrikan viranomaiset peruivat Ajay Guptaa koskeneen pidätysmääräyksen seuraavana vuonna.

Kaksi nuorempaa Gupta-veljestä, Atul ja Rajesh, siirtyivät Arabiemiirikuntiin. Vuonna 2023 paikallinen tuomioistuin hylkäsi Etelä-Afrikan pyynnön heidän luovuttamisestaan.

## Zuma vihjasi paluusta vaaleihin

Zuma oli pitkään valtapuolue ANC:n jäsen, mutta hänet pakotettiin jättämään presidentin tehtävä vuonna 2018 useiden korruptioväitteiden jälkeen. Hän on johdonmukaisesti kiistänyt syyllistyneensä väärinkäytöksiin.

Nykyisin Zuma johtaa uMkhonto weSizwe -puoluetta. Intian-temppelissä tapahtuneen Ajay Guptan tapaamisen jälkeen hänen on kerrottu sanoneen haluavansa asettua ehdolle Etelä-Afrikan seuraavissa vaaleissa. Siksi matka Intiaan ei jäänyt vain yksittäiseksi kuvaksi, vaan se toi uudelleen julkisuuteen vuosia jatkuneen kiistan Zuman, Gupta-veljesten ja Etelä-Afrikan valtion päätöksenteon suhteesta.
summary_bullets: Jacob Zuman ja Ajay Guptan tapaaminen Intiassa on herättänyt uutta arvostelua Etelä-Afrikassa.
Ministeri Khumbudzo Ntshavheni arvosteli tapaamista jyrkästi perjantain tiedotustilaisuudessa.
Gupta-veljekset liittyvät laajaan korruptioskandaaliin, jonka osapuolet ovat kiistäneet väärinkäytökset.
